sermon.title: The New Testament Promise of the Holy Spirit
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer shows that Jesus promised the Holy Spirit to all who thirst, believe and ask—the Comforter, the Spirit of truth and power. He traces the fulfillment through the signs of Mark 16, the day of Pentecost, and later outpourings in Acts, and explains tongues of men and angels and Paul’s “forbid not to speak in tongues.”
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: One phrase at 16:55 was not clear. He says “while Paul spoke” at Cornelius’ house (it was Peter), cites Acts 9:6 for the Ephesus disciples (Acts 19:1–6) and Acts 4:30 for the shaking (4:31). Unchecked: 6,500 languages with 2,050 having the Bible; at least 120 languages at Pentecost; Paul “killed” by stoning and getting up. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Oral Roberts named about the healing ministry, denominations named, beating wives as an example, Pentecostal practices criticized.

chunks.section_question: What did Jesus promise those who thirst?
chunks.short_answer: John 7:37–39: if anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink; whoever believes, out of his innermost being will flow rivers of living water—spoken of the Spirit, not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified. The same belief that brings everlasting life (John 3:16) receives the Holy Spirit.

faqs.question: Is the Holy Spirit only for Pentecostals and charismatics?
faqs.answer: No—the promise is for all followers.

faqs.question: Is spiritual thirst a good thing?
faqs.answer: Yes—a desire for spiritual things and Jesus is God-given even before it is quenched.

faqs.question: Should we pray memorized prayers?
faqs.answer: He says ask for what the Bible says to ask for, and keep on asking.

faqs.question: Does the Spirit run off from you?
faqs.answer: He says the Spirit comes to abide forever; you have to walk away from him.

faqs.question: Which matters most, truth or power?
Who casts out demons?
faqs.answer: We pray and Jesus does it; we are only the vessel.

faqs.question: Should Christians pick up snakes?
faqs.answer: No—that is testing God; Paul’s viper was an accident.

faqs.question: Can God move on people who are sitting?
Is water baptism the same as the baptism of the Holy Ghost?
Why is prophecy preferred over tongues in church?
faqs.answer: Prophecy edifies people; tongues don’t unless interpreted.
